reviewed.title: Under Wildwood
reviewed.author: Colin Meloy
reviewed.summary: I enjoyed the ride that this second installment has taken me on. Of course the narrative did not end neatly, as it’s part of a trilogy. I think that the author broke up the books in a smart way to keep me wanting more. To be…

reviewed.title: Kissing Kosher
reviewed.author: Jean Meltzer
reviewed.summary: I read this on a whim and was surprised by how sensitive and creative a romance book could be. This is my second book that I’ve read by this author and I love the way that she incorporates her protagonist’s chronic illnesses into…

reviewed.title: Adventures from the Land of Stories: The Mother Goose Diaries / Queen Red Riding Hood's Guide to Royalty
reviewed.author: Chris Colfer
reviewed.summary: This set of epistolary tales from the pens of Red Riding Hood and Mother Goose was an excellent audiobook read dramatically by Chris Colfer. I enjoyed the Red Riding Hood story more than the Mother Goose one. Red incorporated…

reviewed.title: 84, Charing Cross Road
reviewed.author: Helene Hanff
reviewed.summary: I appropriately found this book in a Little Free Library on the Upper East Side of Manhattan. This unique epistolary was such a page turner that I felt as though I had been on the mail exchange.

reviewed.title: A Place Between
reviewed.author: Tim Probert
reviewed.summary: As always, Tim Probert produced an amazingly beautiful adventure story for us. Every page was jaw droppingly gorgeous. This installment of the series felt, as the title would suggest, as in between before and after something…

reviewed.title: Playful: How Play Shifts Our Thinking, Inspires Connection, and Sparks Creativity
reviewed.author: Cas Holman
reviewed.summary: I enjoyed reading this manifesto of sorts on having a playful mindset. The stories that Holman provides are joyous and invite the reader to figure out what play means on their own terms.

reviewed.title: The Seven Husbands of Evelyn Hugo
reviewed.author: Taylor Jenkins Reid
reviewed.summary: Seven husbands is too much. This was a fun read. I consumed the pages as if it were a bag of delicious Doritos - a bit salty, a bit bad for you, but certainly fulfilling.

reviewed.title: The Shadow of the Wind
reviewed.author: Carlos Ruiz Zafón
reviewed.summary: This is how books are supposed to be written. It felt like a book I just had to hold in my hands. The plot had so many stories and sub-plots attached to it that it felt like an extremely satisfying and well-written soap opera.…
